_doc: Injection moulding (and, as far as these go, casting in a two-part mould): the mould's halves are drawn off along one axis from a parting plane, so a part optimised for it has no undercuts from either side (the problem's cast: { draw, parting }). Draft is not modelled by the optimiser (a degree or two is less than a cell): add it when the part is drawn. kind community: a moulding service's published guidance; your moulder's figures beat it.
name: mould-injection

draft_per_inch.rule: Rule of thumb: a degree of draft for each inch (25.4 mm) of a cavity's depth, more for deeper features
draft_per_inch.source: Protolabs, Draft Angle Guidelines for Injection Molding, https://protolabs.com/resources/design-tips/improving-part-moldability-with-draft/

draft_min.rule: The least draft worth asking for; 0.25 to 0.5 degrees can work in some cases, confirmed with the moulder first
draft_min.source: Protolabs, Draft Angle Guidelines for Injection Molding, https://protolabs.com/resources/design-tips/improving-part-moldability-with-draft/

draft_shutoff.rule: Least draft where metal slides on metal in the mould (a shutoff)
draft_shutoff.source: Protolabs, Draft Angle Guidelines for Injection Molding, https://protolabs.com/resources/design-tips/improving-part-moldability-with-draft/

draft_texture_light.rule: Draft a lightly textured face needs (PM-T1)
draft_texture_light.source: Protolabs, Draft Angle Guidelines for Injection Molding, https://protolabs.com/resources/design-tips/improving-part-moldability-with-draft/

draft_texture_heavy.rule: Draft a heavily textured face needs (PM-T2), or more
draft_texture_heavy.source: Protolabs, Draft Angle Guidelines for Injection Molding, https://protolabs.com/resources/design-tips/improving-part-moldability-with-draft/
